message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Official EPA air‑quality index (AQI) for all U.S. cities, plus pollutant breakdowns (PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc.). | Enter “Los Angeles” in the search box or use the map. |
| **AQICN** (aqicn.org) | Global AQI with a mobile app and web widget. | Search “Los Angeles” or use the “City” dropdown. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish live updates during smog events. | Look for a “weather” or “environment” section. |
| **Weather apps** (Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) | Many include an AQI indicator. | Open the app, search for Los Angeles, and scroll to the “Air Quality” card. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, here’s a typical example of what you might see:

- **AQI**: 42 (Good)
- **PM₂.₅**: 12 µg/m³ (Moderate)
- **O₃**: 30 ppb (Moderate)
- **NO₂**: 18 ppb (Good)

Keep in mind that AQI values can change rapidly, especially during wildfire season or heat waves. If you have health concerns (e.g., asthma, heart disease), it’s a good idea to stay indoors and keep windows closed when the AQI is above 100.
